newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: "White Australia" policy did not end in 1966.
newsitem.headline: "White Australia" policy did not end in 1966.

text.p: The end of Australia's racist "White Australia" immigration policy in 1966 was in name only as the government continued to discriminate against Asians, secret government documents released on Wednesday showed.

While the then Australian government of prime minister Harold Holt publicly abolished the "White Australia" policy, discrimination against non-Europeans was maintained to ensure the racial composition of immigration did not change.

According to 1966 cabinet papers released by the Australian Archives under a 30-year secrecy rule, the immigration policy was changed only after the cabinet was guaranteed it would still "maintain a predominantly and social homogeneous population".
"The fundamental soundness of a policy directed towards social homogeneity is not in question," said then immigration minister Hubert Opperman in his submission to the cabinet.

On March 2, 1966, the Holt government changed the immigration policy, establishing the principle of admission of selected non-European immigrants, meaning those of Asian origin, on the same basis as those of European heritage.
It also approved a five-year residency period for eligibility for citizenship, replacing the 15-year rule that previously applied to non-Europeans.
In contrast, those of British origin had to wait just 12 months, while others of European origin had to wait five years.
But the change in immigration policy did not end discrimination against Asian migrants, but merely reduced the extent of discrimination.

"The Cabinet wished it to be clear...the basic principles of Australia's immigration policy are not in question, and that no reduction of those principles in any policy sense is intended," a cabinet minute said.
"It follows...that the changes now approved should not be the means of giving rise to new admissions of non-Europeans in large numbers," it said.
Australia has championed the abolition of its "White Australia" policy in its push to integrate into Asia.
The country is embroiled in a race debate after independent politician Pauline Hanson charged in her maiden parliamentary speech that Asians were swamping Australia.
In fact, Asians make up only 4.7 percent of the 18 million population and about one third of the 100,000 annual migrants.
